sections.learningObjectives:
- Describe daily office workflow.
- Trace patient flow from arrival to departure.
- Explain coordination between front and back office.
sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of patient flow like going through a drive-through: you order at the first window (check-in), your food is prepared (exam), and you pay and leave at the last window (check-out). Each step happens in order so nothing gets missed.

### Question 2

Patient flow is like the route you follow through a store: walk in, pick items, pay, and leave. The office plans that route so patients move smoothly from start to finish.

### Question 3

Opening the office is like turning on the lights and checking your mailbox before guests arrive, so you are ready for them.

### Question 4

The front desk person is like the greeter at a restaurant who welcomes you, checks your reservation, and takes your name before you sit down.

### Question 5

When someone arrives, the polite and safe thing is to say hello and make sure you have the right person and know why they came before anything else.

### Question 6

Checking name and birthday is like making sure you hand the right lunchbox to the right student so nobody gets the wrong one.

### Question 7

If someone tells you they moved, you would ask for the new address and write it down correctly rather than leaving the old one or guessing.

### Question 8

Checking insurance is like checking that a gift card still has money on it before you try to use it, so there are no surprises later.

### Question 9

A copayment is like a small entry fee you pay at the door before the visit starts.

### Question 10

When you join a new club, you fill out a membership form first so they know who you are. New patients do the same thing at the doctor's office.

### Question 11

The front desk tells the back office 'your guest is here' using a quiet, reliable signal, like a message, instead of guessing.

### Question 12

The waiting room is like the lobby before a show: a comfortable place to wait until it is your turn.

### Question 13

If someone tells you they feel very sick and their chest hurts, you get help right away instead of telling them to wait.

### Question 14

If a friend shows up late to a planned game, you check whether there is still time to play before deciding what to do.

### Question 15

If someone shows up without a reservation, you look for the next open table rather than slamming the door or making them wait forever.

### Question 16

Rooming is like the person who takes your order and checks your details before the chef (the provider) sees you.

### Question 17

The chief complaint is simply the main thing the patient says is bothering them today.

### Question 18

You would update your contact list whenever someone changes their number, not just the first time you meet them.

### Question 19

Checking allergies is like checking for a food allergy before serving a snack, so you do not give someone something that could hurt them.

### Question 20

The back office quietly taps the provider's shoulder (with a message) to say 'your next patient is ready,' instead of hoping they guess.

### Question 21

The assistant is like the helper who hands tools to the builder: they help, but the builder decides what to build.

### Question 22

You knock before entering someone's room at home, and you do the same at the doctor's office to respect their privacy.

### Question 23

If someone asks for a friend to sit with them because they feel more comfortable, you say yes and arrange it.

### Question 24

Check-out is the last stop, like paying your bill and booking your next haircut before leaving the salon.

### Question 25

The after-visit summary is like a take-home note that reminds you what the doctor said and what to do next.

### Question 26

Booking your next appointment before you leave is like making your next reservation while you are still there, so it is not forgotten.

### Question 27

When the provider says 'please book this patient with a specialist,' the assistant makes the arrangements, just like following a boss's instructions.

### Question 28

Between guests, you clean and reset the room, like wiping a table and resetting it before the next diner sits down.

### Question 29

Washing your hands between patients is like washing your hands before eating: it stops germs from spreading.

### Question 30

If your friend is running late, you would text them to let them know, not leave them guessing.

### Question 31

A bottleneck is like a narrow part of a road where all the cars have to squeeze through slowly, causing a traffic jam behind it.

### Question 32

If the cook takes too long on every dish, the line grows even when everyone else works fast. The slow step is the bottleneck.

### Question 33

If people who booked a table do not show up, the restaurant has empty seats and lost time. No-shows do the same to a doctor's schedule.

### Question 34

A reminder is like a text saying 'see you tomorrow,' so people do not forget to show up.

### Question 35

Buffer time is like leaving early for a trip so a little traffic does not make you late.

### Question 36

Wave scheduling is like seating several guests at once when the restaurant opens, then serving them in order.

### Question 37

Open scheduling is like a store with no appointment times: everyone might come at once, causing a long line.

### Question 38

Double-booking is like telling two friends to come over at the same time, knowing one may have to wait.

### Question 39

If each doctor sees 4 patients an hour and there are 2 doctors, together they see 8 an hour. Over 4 hours, that is 32 patients.

### Question 40

Cycle time is the whole visit on the clock, from walking in the door to walking out.

### Question 41

If a caller sounds very sick, you hand the phone to someone who can help right away, even if you are busy.

### Question 42

A colored flag is like a sticky note that says 'look here!' so the team notices something important.

### Question 43

Checking two identifiers is like checking both the name and the locker number so you open the right locker.

### Question 44

You would not shout someone's secrets in a crowded room; you call just their first name to be discreet.

### Question 45

A privacy screen and a quiet voice are like cupping your hand when whispering so only the right person hears.

### Question 46

The EHR status is like a traffic light telling the team where each patient is in their visit.

### Question 47

You write down a phone number right away so you do not forget it; charting works the same way.

### Question 48

Updating the status to 'done' is like flipping the sign to show that appointment is finished.

### Question 49

If someone feels like they might faint, you help them sit down so they do not fall and get help.

### Question 50

Helping someone in a wheelchair is like helping carry a heavy box: use safe technique and get help if it is too much.

### Question 51

Keeping the path clear and helping someone who is wobbly is like clearing toys off the stairs before Grandma visits.

### Question 52

In an emergency you follow the plan and call for the people who know what to do, like telling a teacher and following the fire drill.

### Question 53

Closing the office is like counting the cash register and tidying up before you lock up for the night.

### Question 54

Setting out everything for tomorrow is like laying out your clothes the night before so the morning is easy.

### Question 55

Reconciling is like checking that the money in the cash box matches what the receipts say you should have.

### Question 56

Checking the day's plan in the morning is like looking at your to-do list before you start, so you are ready.

### Question 57

Keeping rooms stocked is like refilling the pencils and paper in a classroom so the lesson runs smoothly.

### Question 58

When the fridge is almost empty, you add milk to the grocery list before you run out.

### Question 59

When the front and back office work together like a relay team passing the baton, the patient reaches the finish line smoothly.

### Question 60

If two people speak different languages, you bring in a translator so everyone understands, instead of guessing.

### Question 61

A good handoff is like passing a baton with the right note attached: who, why they came, and anything urgent.

### Question 62

If you grab the wrong file, you stop and get the right one right away, because using the wrong one could hurt someone.

### Question 63

Feeling welcome helps people relax and cooperate, which makes everything run more smoothly for everyone.

### Question 64

The back office is like the kitchen where the main work happens, while the front office is the front counter.

### Question 65

Giving a handout is like giving someone a recipe to take home so they remember the steps.

### Question 66

Checking that someone 'got it' is like asking a friend to repeat directions so you know they will not get lost.

### Question 67

If a friend questions a bill, you look at it together and get help if you cannot figure it out.

### Question 68

When the provider says 'order these tests,' the assistant sets it up, like following a recipe the chef has chosen.

### Question 69

In an emergency, the most hurt person gets help first, even if others were waiting longer.

### Question 70

If someone walks slowly, you slow down and help them instead of rushing or sending them away.

### Question 71

A calm, tidy waiting room with friendly updates is like a well-run lobby where everyone knows things are moving.

### Question 72

Checking what checkups are due is like reminding someone their car is due for an oil change.

### Question 73

Room turnover is the cleanup time between guests, like clearing and resetting a table.

### Question 74

Knowing what you are allowed to do and passing the rest to the expert is like calling a plumber instead of fixing the pipes yourself.

### Question 75

When the provider asks for help, the assistant helps, just like handing a tool to someone who is working.

### Question 76

If the number looks off, you tell the person in charge instead of hiding it or guessing it is fine.

### Question 77

Getting an accurate weight is like zeroing a scale before weighing flour so the recipe comes out right.

### Question 78

The provider decides what measurements are needed, and the assistant carries them out, like a helper following a coach's instructions.

### Question 79

The front desk sends a quiet, private message to the right provider's team, like texting 'your guest is here.'

### Question 80

Checking the form is like checking a permission slip is fully filled in before handing it to the teacher.

### Question 81

A work-in is squeezing someone in between appointments when they need to be seen soon.

### Question 82

You fit in the person who needs help most urgently, guided by the rules, not by who pays or who you like.

### Question 83

Marking 'arrived' is like flipping a card to 'here' so everyone knows you showed up.

### Question 84

Getting the address right the first time is like writing the correct address on an envelope so the letter actually arrives.

### Question 85

Before closing up, you check your to-do list and make sure unfinished jobs are noted or handed off, so nothing is forgotten.
